opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (Analyst, full_time) requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; write is not permitted with basic training. Requested write exceeds the maximum allowed, so recommend read.
reason: There is a conflict in the employee facts: HR lists Jennifer Miller (E017) as full_time Analyst, while Security lists her as a contractor with basic security training. Under the contractor policy, basic training permits at most read (write requires advanced training; admin never for contractors), so the requested write exceeds the maximum and should be reduced to read. Choosing the more restrictive maximum is the safe, policy-compliant decision given conflicting employment data; read is also within policy under the full-time interpretation.
